verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission successfully splashed down in the Pacific Ocean off the coast of San Diego, California.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: SPLASHDOWN! NASA’s Artemis II crew... successfully completed a parachute-assisted splashdown in the Pacific Ocean off the coast of San Diego (R1); Pacific Ocean southwest of San Diego (R2); splashed down off the coast of San Diego (R4)
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources directly confirm successful splashdown location in Pacific Ocean off San Diego coast.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission splashed down at 8:07 p.m. EDT on April 10, 2026.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: 8:07 p.m. SPLASHDOWN!... at 8:07 p.m. EDT (5:07 p.m. PDT) (R1); April 10, 5:07:27 p.m. PDT (R2); 8:07 p.m. ET (R4)
verifications.reasoning: Sources explicitly state splashdown at 8:07 p.m. EDT/ET on April 10, 2026 (PDT equivalent confirms).

verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission splashed down at 00:07 UTC on April 11, 2026.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.reasoning: Wikipedia directly states exact time and date in UTC.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission was a 10-day crewed mission around the Moon.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: approximate 10-day mission around the Moon (R1); April 1–11, 2026... crewed lunar flyby (R2); 10-day journey around the moon (R4)
verifications.reasoning: Sources describe it as approximate or 10-day mission around the Moon, matching claim precisely.

verifications.claim: All four crew members of the Artemis II mission are reported in stable condition.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: astronauts are in good shape (R1 snippet); "We are stable. Four green crewmembers" (R4)
verifications.reasoning: Direct report of crew stable and green (good condition) post-splashdown.

verifications.claim: The crew of the Artemis II mission is safely back on Earth.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: The Artemis II crew is safely aboard the USS John P. Murtha (R1); landed them safely back home (R3); astronauts successfully splashed down... back on Earth (R4)
verifications.reasoning: All sources confirm safe return and recovery of crew.

verifications.claim: The Orion capsule of the Artemis II mission was retrieved by the USS John P. Murtha.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: Orion spacecraft is secured in the well deck of USS John P. Murtha (R1); Recovered by USS John P. Murtha (R2); recovery ship, the USS John P. Murtha (R4)
verifications.reasoning: Sources directly state retrieval by USS John P. Murtha.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission marked the first time humans have traveled around the Moon since 1972.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: first crewed flight beyond low Earth orbit since Apollo 17 in 1972... crewed lunar flyby mission
verifications.reasoning: Wikipedia explicitly states first crewed lunar flyby since Apollo 17 (1972).
